Britain lost the American Revolutionary War, then drew the new country's borders generously on purpose. Here's why the 1783 Treaty of Paris looks the way it does.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The treaty was signed in Paris on 3 September 1783 by John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and John Jay for the United States and David Hartley for Britain. It recognised the thirteen former colonies as free, sovereign and independent.

2/ Look at the 1777 side of the map. Britain's Province of Quebec reaches south of the Great Lakes toward the Ohio River, and Spain holds the west. The new United States is a strip along the Atlantic coast.
3/ France's foreign minister Vergennes floated a plan that would have confined the US to land east of the Appalachians. John Jay bypassed him and negotiated directly with Britain's Lord Shelburne.

4/ The deal: the US got everything east of the Mississippi, north of Florida and south of Canada. The northern boundary came out close to today's line. Americans also won fishing rights off Newfoundland and Nova Scotia.

5/ Spain, the war's other big winner, got East and West Florida back in a separate treaty. That one never fixed Florida's northern boundary, which sparked a dispute settled only by the Treaty of Madrid in 1795.
6/ Why so generous? Shelburne wanted to split the US from France and win a profitable trading partner. Historians often note the terms were deliberately favourable to the Americans.
7/ Was Britain's generosity statesmanship, or a bet on trade that paid off? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
